  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 12, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:05 pm in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution
Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493, 2498, 2499 and 2503, due to the continuing state of
emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of
the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Ben Russell.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL AS DMV/DONATE LIFE MONTH

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared April as DMV/Donate Life Month and presented the
Proclamation to One Legacy Ambassador Maria Larson.

B.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL AS EARTHQUAKE PREPAREDNESS
  MONTH

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared April as Earthquake Preparedness Month.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-I AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 12, 2022
 B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF MARCH & APRIL 2022

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64932 THROUGH 65021 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $565,490.94; AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 030622 THROUGH
  030722; IN THE AMOUNT OF $84,840.01; FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $650,330.95 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 8, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 15, 2022

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MARCH 21, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 6, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

I.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - HAWTHORNE BLVD. STORM DRAIN REPAIR
  PROJECT BY E.C. CONSTRUCTION COMPANY

  1) ACCEPTED THE HAWTHORNE BLVD. STORM DRAIN REPAIR
  PROJECT AS COMPLETE; 2) AUTHORIZED THE CITY CLERK TO FILE
  THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION FORM WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  RECORDER’S OFFICE ON APRIL 13, 2022; AND 3) IF NO CLAIMS ARE
  FILED WITHIN 35 DAYS AFTER RECORDATION, DIRECT STAFF TO
  RELEASE THE 5% CONSTRUCTION RETENTION PAYMENT TO E.C.
  CONSTRUCTION IN THE AMOUNT OF $6,856.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

A.  CAL WATER WHITE PAPER AND GENERAL RATE CASE (A.21-07-002)

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file this update.

Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material). She made
two clarifications for the record: 1) on page 2, noting the example non-residential bill is not the
same as the example residential bill, rather it is the revenue requirements; 2) on page 2, the
current litigation is between Cal Water’s contractor and subcontractor, not Cal Water
themselves.

Cal Water representatives in attendance included Angie Gilbride, Carmelo Sorce, Augustin
Baeza and Kevin McCusker. Representative Angie Gilbride provided a presentation
summarizing the 2021 Infrastructure Improvement Plan.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN inquired about the current rates listed in the presentation, and the
potential change in those rates as a result of the current pending litigation. Discussion ensued
about the presented rates, the rate approval process, and how and when these rates could
change as a result of the pending litigation.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 12, 2022
   MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 739 ADDING CHAPTER 16.06 (URBAN LOT
  SPLITS) AND CHAPTER 17.80 (URBAN DWELLING UNITS) TO THE MUNICIPAL
  CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) re-open the Public Hearing on the
  Municipal Code amendments to implement SB-9 pursuant to regular Ordinance No.
  739, take any additional testimony and then close the Public Hearing; and 2) adopt
  Ordinance No. 739.

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 739.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 739 by title.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICES TURF REMOVAL PROGRAM

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Authorize the City to apply for the turf
  removal rebate program through California Water Service for Highridge Park and City
  Hall grounds; 2) Authorize staff to proceed with a Request for Proposals (RFP) for
  landscape design at City Hall; and 3) Appoint a subcommittee to work with staff on the
  scope and design of the project.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted the enthusiasm from the Environmental Advisory
Committee about interest in serving on the subcommittee for this project.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF confirmed that Highridge Park would not require a landscape
architect.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 12, 2022
 Cal Water representative Tammie Myers explained that the idea of the Highridge Park
project would be to transform a high-water use area that isn’t being utilized for any type of
recreation, and reduce water usage in that area. She further explained that both City Hall
and Highridge Park would serve as examples that the community could visit for ideas to
implement in their own yards.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed her appreciation for this program.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked Cal Water for this program. Tammie Myers explained that
there is no end date to the program, and that it was based on available funding, in response
to MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN suggested creating two or three separate garden areas at City Hall
with different designs and plants for the community to visit for inspiration.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) AUTHORIZE THE CITY TO APPLY FOR THE TURF REMOVAL REBATE
  PROGRAM THROUGH CALIFORNIA WATER SERVICE FOR HIGHRIDGE
  PARK AND CITY HALL GROUNDS; 2) AUTHORIZE STAFF TO PROCEED
  WITH A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP) FOR LANDSCAPE DESIGN
  AT CITY HALL; AND 3) APPOINT A SUBCOMMITTEE TO WORK WITH
  STAFF ON THE SCOPE AND DESIGN OF THE PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  REQUEST BY THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA LAND CONSERVANCY TO
  SHARE COSTS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATURE CENTER
  INTERPRETIVE DESIGN

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the City Manager to sign a Letter
  of Agreement with the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy subject to the
  review and approval of the City Attorney for the development of an interpretive design
  for a total cost to the City of $10,000 using Park Facility Fees.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained the important role the Land Conservancy will play in
the development of the interior plans for the building, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN. COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN also confirmed that the Land Conservancy
will continue to be involved in future subcommittee meetings.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF,
  AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO SIGN A LETTER OF AGREEMENT
  WITH THE PALOS VERDES PENINSULA LAND CONSERVANCY SUBJECT
  TO THE REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE CITY ATTORNEY FOR THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF AN INTERPRETIVE DESIGN FOR A TOTAL COST TO
  THE CITY OF $10,000 USING PARK FACILITY FEES.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 12, 2022
 C.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEMS: VARIOUS AREAS OF
  CONCERN; SILVER SPUR ROAD AT RANGE HORSE LANE - STRIPING CONCERN

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the recommendations of the Traffic
  and Safety Committee as outlined in the staff report.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material), and introduced Willdan Traffic Engineer Joanna Itagaki, who summarized
the five items brought forth by the Traffic & Safety Committee.

Engineer Itagaki summarized the first item, “Palos Verdes Peninsula High School – Driveway
2.” Discussion ensued regarding the issue, collision history, and options for traffic modifications.
It was the consensus of the City Council to approve the Traffic & Safety Committee
recommendation to not make any changes at this time, while directing staff to conduct an illegal
turn count, and have the Committee review this item again with more data.

Engineer Itagaki summarized the second item, “Bank of America – 27411 Hawthorne
Boulevard.” Discussion ensued regarding the issue, collision history, and options for traffic
modifications. It was the consensus of the City Council to approve the Traffic & Safety
Committee recommendation to make no change to the existing striping pattern on Hawthorne
Boulevard and revise the exiting arrow in the driveway to a right arrow with the cooperation
with property owner.

Engineer Itagaki summarized the third item, “US Post Office – Deep Valley Drive and Silver
Spur Road.” Discussion ensued regarding the issue and options for traffic modifications. It was
the consensus of the City Council to approve the recommendation of the Traffic & Safety
Committee to make no changes to this area regarding the US Post Office.

Engineer Itagaki summarized the fourth item, “Rancho Vista Elementary School – Palos
Verdes Drive North and Silver Saddle Lane/Moccasin Lane.” Discussion ensued regarding the
issue, collision history and options for traffic modifications. It was the consensus of the City
Council approve the recommendation of the Traffic & Safety Committee to make no changes
to existing traffic controls at this intersection at this time.

Engineer Itagaki summarized the fifth item, “Silver Spur Road at Range Horse Lane - Striping.”
Discussion ensued regarding the issue and options for traffic modifications. It was the
consensus of the City Council to approve the recommendation of the Traffic & Safety
